title: Register Tracer
description: A five-instruction ARM countdown loop stepped one instruction at a time, with live register r0, the zero flag, and an explanation of each executed instruction.
creator: Real-Time DSP on a $5 Microcontroller
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Digital Signal Processing
Assembly Language
Computer Architecture

educational.topic: Tracing an assembly loop and its status flags
learningObjectives: Trace register and flag state one instruction at a time
Interpret how CMP and BNE cooperate through the Z flag
Explain why a label costs nothing at run time

simulationModel.modelType: Instruction-level interpreter with a program counter
equations: BNE: branch taken when Z is clear
assumptions: Only the Z flag is modeled; N, C, and V are not shown
MOV does not affect flags, matching the non-S form
limitations: A single-register example; real assembly juggles many registers and the full flag set

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Instruction-level step-through with concrete state after every step
keyQuestions: Which instruction writes the Z flag and which reads it?
Why does a label execute nothing?
assessmentOpportunities: Predict the behaviour if the CMP instruction were deleted
